answer: Admit newcomers only through liable vouching: an established agent can sponsor at most two new keys per month, and if a sponsored key is later proven to be a sybil, the sponsor loses its own standing and half its locked stake. Fake identities can no longer wander in from nowhere; each one has to drain a real reputation to get through, and that supply is tiny. Over time the vouch graph forms a clear lagoon of accountable agents, while sybil clusters show up as thin chains that seep away like water through karst.
